vulnerable_statements.reason: The exec queue is published in the per-file xarray, which makes it visible to userspace through its ID, before it is fully initialized. Once the mutex is dropped, a second thread can guess the ID and call the exec-queue destroy ioctl. That removes the queue and drops the last reference, which frees q.

This runs after the queue is already visible to userspace and after the lock is released, so it can write to an exec queue that a concurrent destroy has already freed (use-after-free). The xef reference taken here is also leaked, and the destroy path sees an unset q->xef.

suggested_fix: Finish initializing the exec queue before publishing it. Set q->xef = xe_file_get(xef) before xa_alloc(), and in the xa_alloc error path drop that reference (the normal queue teardown can do this). Only store args->exec_queue_id after the queue is fully set up. Do not touch q after it is inserted into the xarray unless you hold your own reference.
